answers.answer: Select number of players + 1 Factory cards randomly, place them face-down on the board, and return the rest unseen. Place one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: randomly select number of players + 1 Factory cards; 11 marked territories; one structure bonus tile; lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.

answers.answer: On the map, put an encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Each player starts with their character at home; two workers on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining home; four mechs over the Faction Mat abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in the Player Mat green boxes marked black; four structures in their matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits on its bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; and the action token beside the Player Mat ready to place. Leave one-time recruit spaces empty. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets popularity, coins, and two objective cards.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 3–4: Faction Mat ... starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat ... popularity, coins and objectives; piece setup table.

answers.answer: You must move your token to a different section, but may take neither action. Rusviet may repeat the prior section; otherwise the section must differ from last turn. If taking both actions, take top before bottom; you cannot take bottom first or return to top afterward. Top-row gains may pay the bottom-row cost. Costs are all exposed red boxes and must be paid in full before the action; green-box benefits are optional and may be taken in any amount. Exact bottom costs and coin benefits depend on the Player Mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: different section; optional top then optional bottom; Rusviet exception; all exposed red boxes; full cost then optional green benefits.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities, and you retain those abilities even without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. You may spend resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: enemy worker alone ... controls it and all its resources; enemy units do not gain ... abilities; spend costs using resources from any territories currently controlled.

answers.answer: No: the normal Move selects up to two different units and moves each one adjacent territory, so one unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A carried worker's carriage is not its own movement, so it may subsequently move itself; a worker may also move onto a mech and be carried by that mech's later move. All units may pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources; only mechs may also carry any number of your workers, and never your character.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: two different units; carried movement does not count as worker's own movement; all units carry resources, mechs also carry workers, never character.

answers.answer: A Speed-enabled mech entering a territory with enemy workers only must stop and cannot move again that turn; those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leave resources behind, and you lose one popularity per worker down to zero. Insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. Your workers cannot independently enter while enemy workers control the territory.
answers.evidence: Enemy workers only: character/mech may enter but stops; workers retreat; lose one popularity per worker, down to zero; workers cannot enter independently.

answers.answer: After all units finish moving in the Move action, resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order when there are multiple combats. Your workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs.
answers.evidence: Enemy character/mechs: finish moving other units, then resolve all combats before bottom-row action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order; workers cannot independently move into or out.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card; an empty combat deck is replenished by shuffling discards, and if both deck and discard are empty you draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity. Traded resources go on a controlled territory containing at least one worker; if all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.
answers.evidence: Bolster and Trade: $1 costs and choices; combat deck recycle; Trade placement and workers-at-home restriction.

answers.answer: Pay all exposed Produce costs (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one token matching its terrain, placed on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and go in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Those workers expose costs for future Produce actions only; they do not change the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce, steps 1–3: pay in full before production; up to two territories; workers from Player Mat left to right; may decline; new costs affect future actions.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in its exposed Upgrade cost boxes, which varies by mat/upgrades; move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost (solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded). Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes, also mat/upgrades dependent; place a Faction Mat mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and all mechs, not workers. Even after completing all such pieces, you may still pay for the bottom action to receive its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade—oil; Deploy—metal and placement; completed bottom actions may still be paid for coins and recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: Build a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker; the Factory is allowed, but lakes and home bases are forbidden, and only one structure total may occupy a territory. Structures cannot be moved or destroyed. A controlled Mill adds a bonus Produce territory; the Mill counts as one producing worker even without an actual worker, and each actual worker there produces normally too. The Mill cannot produce while uncontrolled. Your Mine is a personal tunnel for your unit movement even when its territory is enemy-controlled; an enemy occupant does not remove your Mine ability.
answers.evidence: Build: placement restrictions and structures cannot move/destroy; Mill can produce without actual worker, only while controlled; Mine is personal tunnel even when enemy-controlled.

answers.answer: Put the recruit permanently on any open one-time bonus space on your Faction Mat and immediately take that space's bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is determined by the Player Mat circle uncovered where the recruit was removed: Upgrade gives one power, Deploy one coin, Build one popularity, Enlist one combat card. Resolve the active player first, then immediate left, then immediate right, stopping if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play the opponent triggers the bonus once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits: Faction Mat one-time bonus, circle uncovered determines ongoing type, order and two-player rule.

answers.answer: Combatants simultaneously and secretly select dial power from zero to the smaller of seven and current power, and may each add up to one combat card per participating character/mech (Rusviet People's Army adds one card total if any workers are present). When both combatants have combat mech abilities, attacker resolves theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial plus card values; attacker wins ties. Both pay by deducting selected dial power from the Power Track and discarding each played card face-up; card value does not deduct additional track power.
answers.evidence: Combat, steps 1–4: simultaneously and secretly; dial cap; optional cards; attacker abilities first; reveal simultaneously; attacker wins ties; both pay.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and resources. Losing characters, mechs, and workers all retreat to their own home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy allows eligible units and carried workers to retreat to an adjacent lake instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat (including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake); a winning defender loses none, with Polania Camaraderie's stated combat exception. A non-Saxony winner with zero or one combat star places one; with two, none. Saxony places one for each victory while star tokens remain. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed any power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser gets none.
answers.evidence: Combat, steps 5–6: winner controls; losing units retreat leaving resources; popularity loss; combat-star award; loser card reward.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on the token territory; discard token and draw a card. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token remains. Gains go to the encounter territory. Pay only the selected option's printed cost; there are no additional normal action costs or mat benefits, including ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Encounters: after whole Move action and all combats; if contested entry lost token stays; gains go to encounter territory; no additional costs or mat benefits.

answers.answer: Each player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed), looks at available Factory cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. This applies to every player, not only the first visitor; each player gets at most one permanent card and later visits cannot exchange it. It is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom under the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception). Factory actions do not grant corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories, or three for a Speed character/mech, with Mine access and ordinary movement/stop rules applying.
answers.evidence: Factory: every player's character first finish; one permanent card; fifth action; no corresponding bonuses; bottom action movement and Speed.

answers.answer: Reveal a completed objective only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, and meet all requirements at the moment of reveal. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is available; Saxony retains the other card after the first and can score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: own turn timing, all requirements at reveal, both cards discarded to bottom; Saxony exception.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. A placed star is permanent even if power or popularity later drops, and another player's star never blocks a goal. The sixth star immediately ends play, with no further turns or actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end: achievements, once-only exceptions, permanent stars, other players do not block, sixth star ends immediately.

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect its primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement and return initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat. For a neighbor recruit star, finish the active action, then check active player first, left neighbor, right neighbor; if an earlier player places the sixth star, no later recruit star or bonus resolves.
answers.evidence: Sixth star sequence: bottom action benefits before star; unresolved battle movement undone; neighbor order and stop condition.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity the 7–12 tier applies: five stars add $20 ($4 each); four normal territories plus Factory count as seven territories and add $21 ($3 each); 13 controlled resources make six complete pairs and add $12 ($2 each). These add $53 to held coins, before any structure bonus. Your structures qualify for the selected structure bonus even if enemies control their territories. Victory ties break by workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, controlled resources, controlled territories, and stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune: 7–12 tier payouts; Factory counts three; resources as complete pairs; structure eligibility; tiebreak order.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for game effects. Normally you cannot move into any home base; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea's unlocked Wayfare. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: home base not a territory; entry exceptions; unmatched bases are inactive expansion placeholders.

answers.answer: Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers; lakes and the Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table; resources section: only wood, food, metal and oil are resources; no supply limit, use multipliers.

answers.answer: Any unit may pick up, carry, or drop resources mid-movement; a mech may also pick up/carry/drop your workers, but may never carry your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step, with Speed's extra step available before or after it. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move: units carry resources and mechs workers; Speed; tunnel jump costs one; enemy and encounter stops override Speed.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory containing only an enemy structure and take control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Move: Enemy structure only; all printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.

answers.answer: Do not pay a partial Produce cost. If unable to afford any action, take a legal dead turn: move the token to a different section and take neither action.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: full cost; never pay only part; dead turn by moving token to a different section and taking neither action.

answers.answer: A built Armory grants one power whenever you take Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity whenever you take Bolster. You retain structure abilities even without control of their territories, and enemy units do not gain them; the Mill is the stated exception that cannot produce while uncontrolled.
answers.evidence: Bolster/Trade building bonuses; control section: keep abilities without control, except Mill production; enemy units do not gain abilities.

answers.answer: Riverwalk is an unlockable mech ability for every faction and lets the character and all mechs, not workers, cross rivers to these destinations: Nordic and Saxony forests and mountains; Rusviet farms and villages; Crimea farms and tundra; Polania villages and mountains. Nordic's starting Swim lets workers alone cross rivers to land terrain, not lakes. Swim does not grant lake movement to Nordic mechs; Nordic's separate Seaworthy ability does that for character/mechs.
answers.evidence: Riverwalk destinations table; Nordic Swim and Seaworthy descriptions.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including its Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. These shortcuts are for characters and mechs, not workers.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township descriptions specify character/mech Move actions.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or Saxony's Mine: the opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery also applies before combat, but Nordic may pay one power to reduce the opponent's power by two; likewise once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Saxony Underpass/Disarm and Nordic Artillery descriptions.

answers.answer: Two mechs and three workers may play three combat cards total with People's Army: the usual one per participating character/mech plus one additional card total when at least one worker is present. Workers alone never fight.
answers.evidence: Rusviet People's Army: one additional card total with worker present; two mechs and three workers allow three cards; workers alone never fight.

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare lets its character/mechs move from a territory or home base to Crimea's own or any inactive faction home base, regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. They cannot move to an active opponent's home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare description: own or inactive home base; not active opponent base.

answers.answer: Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into its hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion lets Crimea spend one combat card as any one resource, regardless of the card's value, once per turn.
answers.evidence: Crimea Scout and starting Coercion descriptions.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake, but gives no adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes need a mech to move off. A carrier leaving a lake cannot leave carried workers or resources behind.
answers.evidence: Nordic Seaworthy and Polania Submerge descriptions; lake carrier rule.

answers.answer: Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn. It does not prevent popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Polania Camaraderie: combat aggressor exception; not undefended-worker drive-off.

answers.answer: Polania resolves one drawn encounter card by choosing up to two different options from that card, in either order. The first option’s gain can pay the second option’s cost.
answers.evidence: Polania Meander: choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; first gain can pay second cost.

answers.answer: No. A character entering an encounter territory stops and cannot move again that turn, including during Factory Move. The encounter is resolved only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there.
answers.evidence: Move: character entering encounter stops; Encounters: after whole Move action and all combats; Factory rules say same rules apply.

answers.answer: Coins are not hidden information, but you need not reveal their exact total when asked. Combat-card hand count is public, while contents are secret until revealed; during combat you may conceal whether you committed any cards until reveal. Objective contents are secret until you reveal a completed objective.
answers.evidence: Public and hidden information table: combat-card hand count and concealment exception; objectives; coins.

answers.answer: Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable; agreements are informal and unenforceable. In tournament play, even coin exchanges for deals/alliances are forbidden. A payment cannot cancel combat once movement has placed units onto opposing units; combat must occur after Move, though bribes may influence its outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: coins only tangible items exchangeable; unenforceable; combat cannot be canceled after initiated by movement.

answers.answer: Popularity 0–6 scores $3 per star, $2 per territory counted, and $1 per complete pair of controlled resources. Popularity 7–12 scores $4, $3, and $2 respectively. Popularity 13–18 scores $5, $4, and $3 respectively. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Only complete resource pairs score, so a single leftover resource scores nothing.
answers.evidence: Final fortune popularity table; controlled lakes count and home bases do not; resource income counts complete pairs rounded down.

answers.answer: For adjacency bonuses, count each qualifying feature uniquely across all your structures; rivers do not break adjacency. Count printed tunnel territories, not Mines; count unique lakes; count unique printed encounter locations even if their token has been removed. The payouts for 1 / 2–3 / 4–5 / 6 features are $2 / $4 / $6 / $9 for adjacent tunnels; adjacent encounters use $2 / $4 / $6 / $9 for 1 / 2–3 / 4–5 / 6–7; adjacent lakes likewise use $2 / $4 / $6 / $9 for 1 / 2–3 / 4–5 / 6–7.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility table: tunnels, lakes and encounters; unique features, removed tokens, Mines excluded, rivers do not break adjacency.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels count structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, and 3–4 pays $6. Structures in a row score only the longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break the line. One, two, three, or four structures in that line pay $2, $4, $6, or $9. Structures on farms/tundras count qualifying structures combined; one, two, three, or four pay $2, $4, $6, or $9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility table: structures on tunnels, structures in a row, structures on farms/tundras.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
answers.evidence: Combat step 6: popularity loss includes workers carried by defeated mech on a lake.

answers.answer: No. A popularity star is permanent if popularity later drops, but current popularity still determines final scoring. Another player's star never blocks the same goal, so different factions may each earn that achievement.
answers.evidence: Stars: placed star permanent, current popularity determines final scoring, other players' stars never block a goal.

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order clockwise: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Seating identifies each player's immediate left and right neighbors, whose qualifying bottom-row actions can trigger ongoing recruit bonuses; resolve active player, then left, then right.
answers.evidence: Setup: random mat deal and faction board order; Ongoing recruits: immediate left/right neighbors trigger bonuses.

answers.answer: A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability may enter the lake from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
answers.evidence: Move: river definition; lake occupies hex and extends to adjacent shoreline; entry from any surrounding land territory adjoining shores.

answers.answer: No. Show the encounter card to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud. You need not read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounters: show card to all players, show artwork, read capitalized thematic text aloud; options need not all be read.

answers.answer: No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: no limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.

answers.answer: The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: next clockwise player may begin while current player decides which item to gain after starting a noninteractive bottom action.

answers.answer: No. The chosen top and bottom actions are each limited to once within the turn, including for Rusviet; its repeat ability waives only the previous-turn section restriction.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: chosen top and bottom actions each limited to once within turn, including Rusviet.

answers.answer: You may gain $1 instead of moving units with the normal unupgraded Move action.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: alternatively gain $1.

answers.answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat, including after retreat; new workers are taken from the mat left to right and placed in a producing village.
answers.evidence: Produce: workers never return to Player Mat; workers on retreat go to home base.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity.
answers.evidence: Combat: you may attack with zero power/popularity.

answers.answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching the non-Saxony combat-star limit; a non-Saxony winner with two combat stars places no additional combat star.
answers.evidence: Combat star award: after two stars places none; may still fight after reaching combat-star limit.

answers.answer: A faction without Meander must choose one affordable option and cannot decline to choose. It cannot select an unaffordable coin/popularity option. After paying the printed cost, it may take as little of the selected option's benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Encounters: must choose one affordable option; unaffordable options cannot be selected; may take as little benefit as desired.

answers.answer: No. Combatants choose their dials simultaneously and secretly, not in turn order. Dials and selected cards are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1 and 3: simultaneously and secretly choose; reveal simultaneously.

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: No. Place a star as soon as you achieve its goal; a placed star is permanent and the sixth star immediately ends play. A completed objective is different: you may wait to reveal it, but reveal only on your own turn and only while meeting all its requirements.
answers.evidence: Stars: place as soon as achieved and sixth star ends; Objectives: may wait, but own-turn reveal and meet requirements at reveal.

answers.answer: Normally, units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. Faction and mech abilities provide the exceptions.
answers.evidence: Move: units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes; abilities provide exceptions.

answers.answer: No. The recruit is permanently placed on the chosen open one-time bonus space and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist: put recruit permanently on any open one-time bonus; it cannot later move.

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a mech or worker entering that territory does not trigger or remove its token.
answers.evidence: Encounters: only a character triggers an encounter.

answers.answer: While you control the Mill territory, it adds one bonus producing territory to the normal allowance: up to three total with a normal two-territory allowance, or up to four with an upgraded allowance of three. The Mill itself counts as one producing worker and produces the terrain's matching token even with no actual worker there; each actual worker in the Mill territory also produces normally, so the Mill adds output rather than replacing worker output.
answers.evidence: Produce: controlled Mill provides one bonus territory; Mill counts as worker and can produce without actual worker; actual workers also produce.

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish or preserve control after your last unit leaves if you have no structure there.
answers.evidence: Control: a territory is controlled by your unit or your structure with no enemy unit; resources alone are not listed as control.

answers.answer: Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
answers.evidence: Bottom resources: Upgrade oil; Deploy metal; Build wood; Enlist food.
